arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Barnard argued for Zadvydas. He stated Zadvydas is stateless. He argued the detention is indefinite. He claimed the law does not support this outcome.
Mr. Stansell argued for the government. He stated the administrative process is flawed. He argued deportation is not foreseeable. He claimed the law requires continued detention.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kestutis Zadvydas arrived in the United States as a stateless person. He remains stateless. The government detained him. His lawyers argue this detention violates the law. The government argues the law requires detention until removal is possible.

paragraphs: This case defines the limits of executive power over non-citizens. It determines whether the government can hold people without a realistic prospect of removal. It impacts the rights of stateless individuals in the United States.
